text: Ask HN: What do you run on a $5 VPS that's worth keeping online 24/7? | Hacker News Hacker News new | past | comments | ask | show | jobs | submit login Ask HN: What do you run on a $5 VPS that's worth keeping online 24/7? 17 points by mariocesar 8 hours ago | hide | past | favorite | 11 comments DHH's "AI shed" idea got me thinking about getting a small $5–10/month VPS. I'm a Linux guy and have on many points of my life have a personal server. So I like the idea of having something always on, but I’m not sure the maintenance is worth it when most things can just run on my laptop. That said, I tend to do things myself and only later realize I could have automated or delegated them, so I may have a blind spot here. If you have a cheap VPS or mini PC, what actually ended up being useful long-term? Anything that saved enough time or replaced enough subscriptions to justify keeping it around? ehe78qhe 48 minutes ago | next [–] On my home server (just an older desktop PC) - qBittorrent for "Linux ISOs" - Jellyfin so I can watch/read/listen to my "Linux ISOs" - Tailscale so me, my family and friends can watch/read/listen to my "Linux ISOs" from anywhere in the world - Self hosting my photo albums. Immich is a handy choice for this. Very useful for personal photos you don't want to trust to strange tech companies. - Gitea for self-hosting git repos for some personal projects I have not open-sourced. reply cutthegrass2 21 minutes ago | prev | next [–] a container image with a wireguard server plus a bunch of host configuration scripts to automate the setup. Handy to have a non commercial VPN solution you can deploy in any region. reply jbarberu 3 hours ago | prev | next [–] I recently closed down a VPS I had been running for the last 10 years. Mostly used it for hosting a personal website and some smaller other static sites, as well as git repo backups. After getting into home assistant and setting up a proper home server I no longer saw a need to keep the VPS running. With cloudflare reverse proxy I can still host personal websites, but from inside my home network. Since getting the home server I'm discovering a lot of neat self hosted options and use it a lot more than I ever did the VPS. If nothing else, hosting your own stuff provides a great place to learn and explore. It doesn't have to be always on/on the internet for that to be true though. reply sebnun 5 hours ago | prev | next [–] I run a language learning app* on a single VPS, for free. I'm not sure if you can still get it, but Oracle used to offer very generous VPS for free. I have a 4 CPUs, 24 GB memory VPS that I'm using for several things, including running the backend and the marketing site for that app. I installed Plex but ended up not using it, so I removed it. * https://www.langturbo.com reply spl757 2 hours ago | prev | next [–] dns and email server. i just make aliases that point to a single imap account that is unique for everything i sign up for. if i start to get spam, turn off the alias. it also lets me see who is selling my info or has been hacked when bestbuy@example.com starts getting emails from russia. reply ogou 3 hours ago | prev | next [–] Messaging queues and brokers. RabbitMQ, BullMQ, etc. Simple services, but I've learned to keep them on their own images so they recover fast and don't compete with other resources. reply dare944 6 hours ago | prev | next [–] Mail / IMAP server for my family domain. Small web server with a few static content sites. Trillium notes server. Pretty low maintenance overall - I can go months without even thinking about it. reply 1vuio0pswjnm7 4 hours ago | prev | next [–] 1. Authoritative DNS server 2.
